why: The question asks a quarterly figure (Q4 2027 against Q4 2026), not a year's figure, so the code-set day 2028-03-30 (90 days after calendar 2027) does not apply, and the thesis puts the Q4 2027 releases at roughly January 2028.

The question asks a survey share for the rolling twelve months from 2026-07-07 to 2027-07-07, not a calendar year's figure, and no publication day is given; the due day 2027-07-07 is only the period's last day, neither a publication date nor the code-set day, so due_day_basis "expected_publication" is untrue.
The article states NVIDIA will file its fiscal 2027 Form 10-K on February 24, 2027, so the due day 2027-04-01 contradicts that date, and due_day_basis should be "stated", not "expected_publication".

The question asks a survey share for the twelve months after 2026-07-07 (to about mid-2027), not calendar 2026's figure, so the code-set day 2027-03-31 (90 days after calendar 2026) falls before the figure's period ends.

The thesis says the price is checked against Ornn's published spot index at year-end 2026, and the question measures it on 2026-12-31, so the due day 2027-03-31 (code's 90-day lag for a whole year's figure) contradicts the stated check date, and due_day_basis "expected_publication" is untrue.
